name: Closing-Imbalance Window Momentum
note: Rides the price reaction to the 15:50 ET closing-auction imbalance publication into the print. The regular-session open is located from the data (modal max-volume bar of each session's first half), the close bar is the last bar inside open+390 minutes, and the move over the bars straddling the publication is compared with its own trailing percentile plus a volume-participation test. Entry on the following bar's open, exit at the close bar's close, never overnight. The $50m dollar-volume floor is a universe filter, not a bar rule, so it is left to the study's symbol list. The only sample-wide quantity is the modal regular-session open minute, a clock constant (9:30 ET) inferred from timestamps rather than prices; every price and volume input to the signal is strictly past.
source: Synthesis. Grounded in the published exchange mechanics - NYSE and Nasdaq begin disseminating closing-auction imbalance information at 15:50 ET - and in the closing-auction price-discovery literature. The three-minute price-reaction proxy for the unobservable imbalance feed is my construction; no paper states this exact rule.
